Is it better to take out a new policy?
What costs are involved with switching car insurance from one car to another?
How can I pay for any charges?
What’s the process of changing car insurance?
When do I need to arrange the change?
Buying a new car is exciting – buying insurance, not so much!
But car insurance is a super important part of car ownership and switching your existing policy over to your new car is simple and easy.
Our handy guide explains how it works, how much it works, and the information you’ll need to hand.
It’s important to check you can afford your new car insurance before you buy the car, so try to get a quote on the change in advance.
Even if the new car is worth less, has a smaller engine or is older than the one it’s replacing, your insurance could go up in price.
Older cars can fall into higher car insurance groups as they have fewer safety and security features, making claims either more likely, or more expensive when they do happen.
Give as much information as possible when getting your quote.
A registration number will usually tell us about the make, model, engine size and trim level, but we’ll also ask you about modifications.
If you’ve not found an exact car and don’t have a registration number, you should decide on an exact model in advance.
Two similar vehicles can be priced very differently because of differences in engine size or specification.
Arranging a brand new policy for your new car would mean cancelling your old one midway through, and that can incur cancellation charges.
It could also mean losing the year’s no claims bonus that you’re in the process of building up.
So it may make more sense to wait until renewal time before shopping around.
Your insurer will calculate the difference in price between the old car and the new one on a 12-month basis, then work out how much to charge on a pro-rata basis, down to the day.
On top of this, an administration fee is charged to cover the cost of updating your policy and updating the Motor Insurance Database.
You’ll have to pay for any change in the same way you paid for your policy when you first bought it (or last renewed, whichever is the more recent).
So, if you’re paying monthly already, you’ll be able to spread the cost over any instalments that haven’t yet been collected.
If you've paid for the policy in full the additional premium will be taken from the credit/debit card details we hold on file.
You can arrange to amend your insurance policy with us over the phone or online.
If you’re doing it online you’ll need to have a few details to hand, including your policy number.
You’ll be asked to provide a few details, including the car’s registration number and when you want the change to take place.
Once you’ve accepted that and arranged payment, we’ll generate a new set of documents for you, including a certificate of motor insurance and a schedule.
On the day of the car insurance transfer, there’s a little flexibility about when the switchover happens.
The cover on the new vehicle/the cover on the old vehicle will start/stop as soon as you step inside the new vehicle.
Remember, you may be charged a fee for this. When you take out a policy with us, you’ll be sent a document ‘Your Agreement with EUI Limited’, which will let you know how much this might be.
Or, you can chat to one of our agents who will let you know.
When you buy any car, you’ll need to arrange road tax. You can buy this online as long as you have a copy of the new keeper supplement from the car’s logbook.
When you come to do this, you’ll need to have insurance in place for when the tax is set to start.
Computer systems need a little time to update, so it’s a good idea to arrange the switchover at least the day before you collect the new car.
That said, cover can be changed immediately if you buy a new car on the spur of the moment.
While it’s nice to imagine every car we buy is going to be reliable, there are no guarantees.
So, think hard about whether to take out breakdown cover, especially if a car is second-hand and you don’t know its history.
At Admiral, breakdown cover is included as standard on our Platinum tier, or it can be bought as an add-on on our other levels of cover.
If you’re buying a used car read our handy checklist to make sure you ask all the right questions.
